technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot and Spring Kafka for Kafka integration to leverage built-in configuration and messaging templates.
Use Spring's @ConfigurationProperties to implement global configuration options as defaults with per-deployment overrides.
Implement concurrency and compression using Kafka producer/consumer properties and Spring's concurrent message listener containers.
Use Spring Integration or Reactor Kafka to implement bindRequestor and bindReplier for asynchronous request-reply patterns.
Interact with Sqoop using its Java API or CLI execution via ProcessBuilder to manage jobs and retrieve logs.
Use Logback or Log4j2 with an appropriate Appender to capture and stream Sqoop logs to the central logging mechanism.
Use Testcontainers in the CI pipeline to provide ephemeral Kafka and Sqoop instances for acceptance tests.
assumptions: The existing codebase is a Spring Boot application running on Java 17+.
The CI environment supports Docker for running Testcontainers.
Sqoop is accessible from the application environment either via API or CLI.
The developer has prior experience with Spring Framework, Kafka, and Sqoop.
Standard logging mechanisms (e.g., ELK stack or similar) are already in place to receive streamed logs.

activities.activity_description: Analyze user stories, design the architecture for Kafka and Sqoop integrations, and define configuration structures.
Set up Testcontainers for Kafka and write acceptance tests to validate message bus functionality in CI builds.
Implement global default configurations and per-deployment overrides for concurrency and compression in Kafka producers and consumers.
Implement message acknowledgement options to guarantee successful message/request delivery.
Implement functionality to bind a producer expecting async replies and a consumer handling requests to asynchronously send replies.
Implement batching options for Kafka producers and consumers to ingest data in batches instead of one payload at a time.
Implement the ability to stop an existing Sqoop job to clean up resources upon completion.
Identify how to capture Sqoop logs and stream them to the application's logging mechanism for troubleshooting.
Implement incremental data load functionality to retrieve only rows newer than previously imported data.
Integrate all components, perform end-to-end testing, update documentation, and finalize CI/CD pipeline configurations.
